title: ChatGPT Business Hub Launches With Core Update & AI Mode
summary: OpenAI unveils ChatGPT Business Hub with core platform updates and AI Mode's new model. Professional workspace tools now available for enterprise teams.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- OpenAI launched ChatGPT Business Hub on November 14, 2026, consolidating enterprise workspace tools into a unified platform.
- The update includes core infrastructure improvements and a new underlying model powering AI Mode for business users.
- Business Hub targets professional teams with enhanced collaboration features, custom workflows, and enterprise-grade security controls.


OpenAI officially launched ChatGPT Business Hub on November 14, 2026, introducing a unified enterprise workspace that consolidates professional tools, team collaboration features, and administrative controls into a single platform. The release includes significant core infrastructure updates and debuts a new model architecture powering AI Mode for business users, marking a strategic shift toward serving organizational customers at scale.


## What ChatGPT Business Hub Delivers


The Business Hub platform provides companies with a centralized dashboard for managing ChatGPT access across teams. Organizations can now provision user accounts, set usage policies, configure data retention rules, and monitor activity through a single administrative interface. The hub supports role-based permissions, allowing administrators to define custom access levels for different departments or project groups.


Integration capabilities form a core component of the offering. Business Hub connects with existing enterprise software through pre-built connectors for platforms like Slack, Microsoft Teams, and Google Workspace. Companies can deploy ChatGPT functionality directly within their existing workflows without requiring employees to switch between applications.


## Core Infrastructure Updates


The platform launch accompanies substantial backend improvements to ChatGPT's core systems. OpenAI reports enhanced response latency, with average generation speeds improving by 40 percent compared to previous enterprise deployments. The update also introduces improved context handling, allowing Business Hub users to maintain longer conversation threads with better coherence across extended interactions.


Security enhancements include end-to-end encryption for all business conversations, compliance certifications for SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 standards, and data residency options for organizations subject to regional privacy regulations. OpenAI commits that Business Hub customer data will not be used for model training, addressing a persistent concern among enterprise buyers.


## AI Mode's New Model Architecture


Business Hub users gain access to an upgraded AI Mode powered by a refined model architecture optimized for professional use cases. According to OpenAI, the new model demonstrates improved performance on business-specific tasks including technical documentation synthesis, financial data analysis, and legal contract review. Benchmark testing shows a 25 percent accuracy gain on domain-specific reasoning tasks compared to the previous generation.


The model introduces adaptive behavior tuning, allowing organizations to configure AI Mode's output style and formality level to match their corporate communication standards. Companies can establish custom knowledge bases that the model references when responding to queries, ensuring outputs align with internal policies and proprietary information.


## Release Date and Availability


ChatGPT Business Hub officially launched on November 14, 2026, with immediate availability for enterprise customers. Organizations can access the platform through annual subscription plans starting at $30 per user per month for teams of 10 or more. OpenAI offers a 30-day trial period for companies evaluating the service before committing to a full deployment.


The rollout follows a three-month private beta program involving approximately 200 enterprise customers across technology, financial services, and healthcare sectors. Participating organizations provided feedback that shaped the final feature set and pricing structure.


## What This Means


The Business Hub launch represents OpenAI's most comprehensive enterprise offering to date, directly competing with Microsoft's Copilot for Microsoft 365 and Google's Workspace AI features. By bundling administrative tools, security controls, and an optimized model into a single package, OpenAI addresses the operational complexity that has limited broader ChatGPT adoption in regulated industries. The platform's emphasis on data sovereignty and compliance certifications signals an intent to capture market share among risk-averse enterprise buyers who have delayed AI deployment pending robust governance frameworks. For organizations already using ChatGPT informally, Business Hub provides a path to formalize usage with appropriate oversight and control mechanisms.
